units.title: Numbers to 1,000
units.blurb: Round, estimate, and add and subtract three-digit numbers with confidence.

units.title: What Multiplication Means
units.blurb: See multiplication as equal groups and arrays, and learn the facts with strategies.

units.title: What Division Means
units.blurb: See division as sharing and as making groups, and connect it to multiplication.

units.title: Word Problems and Patterns
units.blurb: Choose the operation, model the problem, and check the answer.

units.title: Fractions
units.blurb: Understand fractions as equal parts, place them on the number line, and compare them.

units.title: Time, Mass and Liquid Volume
units.blurb: Tell time to the minute, find elapsed time, and measure mass and volume.

units.title: Area and Perimeter
units.blurb: Measure the space inside a shape and the distance around it.

units.title: Graphs and Line Plots
units.blurb: Read and make scaled graphs, and show measurements on a line plot.

units.title: Shapes
units.blurb: Sort shapes by their attributes and see that categories overlap.

topics.title: Rounding to the Nearest 10 or 100
topics.short: Find the closest ten or hundred to a number.
topics.trouble: Students look at the wrong digit, or think a number like 450 rounds down because 5 is "in the middle."

topics.title: Adding within 1,000
topics.short: Add three-digit numbers, regrouping ones and tens when needed.
topics.trouble: Students forget to add the regrouped ten or hundred, or line up digits by the left edge instead of by place.

topics.title: Subtracting within 1,000
topics.short: Subtract three-digit numbers, regrouping when a digit is too small.
topics.trouble: Students subtract the smaller digit from the larger in each column, so 352 − 178 comes out as 226.

topics.title: Subtracting Across Zeros
topics.short: Regroup through a zero, as in 400 − 127.
topics.trouble: When the tens digit is 0, students borrow from the hundreds but forget to turn the 0 tens into 9 tens.

topics.title: Estimating Sums and Differences
topics.short: Round first to check whether an answer makes sense.
topics.trouble: Students treat an estimate as a wrong answer and skip it, so they never catch a regrouping slip.

topics.title: Equal Groups
topics.short: 3 × 4 means 3 groups with 4 in each group.
topics.trouble: Students add the numbers instead of multiplying, so 3 groups of 4 becomes 7.

topics.title: Arrays
topics.short: Rows and columns of objects show a multiplication.
topics.trouble: Students count every dot one by one instead of seeing rows of the same size.

topics.title: Turn-Around Facts
topics.short: 3 × 5 and 5 × 3 have the same product.
topics.trouble: Students think 3 × 5 and 5 × 3 are different problems they must learn separately.

topics.title: Multiplying by 0 and 1
topics.short: Any number times 0 is 0; any number times 1 is itself.
topics.trouble: Students write 6 × 0 = 6 because they mix up multiplying by 0 with adding 0.

topics.title: Facts of 2, 5 and 10
topics.short: Use doubles and skip counting for these facts.

topics.title: Facts of 3, 4 and 6
topics.short: Build these facts by doubling and adding a group.

topics.title: Breaking Apart a Fact
topics.short: Split 7 × 6 into 5 × 6 plus 2 × 6.
topics.trouble: Students split one factor but multiply only one part by the other factor, so 7 × 6 becomes 5 × 6 + 2.

topics.title: Facts of 7, 8 and 9
topics.short: Learn the hardest facts with patterns and break-apart strategies.

topics.title: Grouping Factors
topics.short: Multiply three numbers in any grouping, like (2 × 5) × 7.

topics.title: Multiplying by Multiples of 10
topics.short: 4 × 30 is 4 groups of 3 tens, so 12 tens.
topics.trouble: Students learn "just add a zero" without knowing why, which later breaks with decimals.

topics.title: Division as Fair Sharing
topics.short: Share a total equally to find how many in each group.

topics.title: Division as Making Groups
topics.short: Find how many groups of a given size fit in a total.
topics.trouble: Students mix up the two meanings and cannot tell whether the answer counts groups or items in a group.

topics.title: Division as a Missing Factor
topics.short: 24 ÷ 6 asks what times 6 makes 24.

topics.title: Fact Families
topics.short: Three numbers give two multiplication and two division facts.

topics.title: Dividing with 0 and 1
topics.short: 0 divided by a number is 0, but you cannot divide by 0.
topics.trouble: Students think 5 ÷ 0 is 0 or 5, not seeing that no number times 0 gives 5.

topics.title: Finding the Unknown Number
topics.short: Find the missing number in 8 × ? = 48 or 35 ÷ ? = 5.
topics.trouble: Students read the equals sign as "the answer comes next" and write the product instead of the missing factor.

topics.title: Multiplication and Division Word Problems
topics.short: Decide whether a story is about groups, sharing or arrays.
topics.trouble: Students hunt for key words like "each" instead of picturing the situation, and so choose the wrong operation.

topics.title: Using a Letter for the Unknown
topics.short: Write an equation with a letter standing for the number you want.

topics.title: Two-Step Word Problems
topics.short: Solve a problem that needs two operations, then check with an estimate.
topics.trouble: Students do only the first step and report that partial result as the answer.

topics.title: Patterns in the Tables
topics.short: Explain patterns in addition and multiplication tables.

topics.title: Equal Parts of a Whole
topics.short: A fraction needs the whole split into parts of equal size.
topics.trouble: Students call any split a fraction, even when the parts are not the same size.

topics.title: Unit Fractions
topics.short: 1/4 is one of 4 equal parts of a whole.
topics.trouble: Students think 1/8 is bigger than 1/4 because 8 is bigger than 4.

topics.title: Building Fractions from Unit Fractions
topics.short: 3/4 is three pieces of size 1/4.
topics.trouble: Students read the numerator and denominator as two separate whole numbers instead of one amount.

topics.title: Unit Fractions on the Number Line
topics.short: Split the space from 0 to 1 into equal parts.
topics.trouble: Students count the tick marks instead of the spaces between them, so fourths look like fifths.

topics.title: Fractions on the Number Line
topics.short: Mark 3/4 by counting 3 lengths of 1/4 from 0.
topics.trouble: Students start counting at the first tick after 0 instead of at 0.

topics.title: Whole Numbers as Fractions
topics.trouble: Students believe a fraction is always less than 1.

topics.title: Equivalent Fractions
topics.short: 1/2 and 2/4 name the same point and the same amount.
topics.trouble: Students think 2/4 is bigger than 1/2 because its numbers are bigger.

topics.title: Comparing Fractions with the Same Denominator
topics.short: Same-size pieces: more pieces means more.

topics.title: Comparing Fractions with the Same Numerator
topics.short: Same number of pieces: bigger pieces means more.
topics.trouble: Students pick the fraction with the bigger denominator as larger, carrying over a whole-number habit.

topics.title: Telling Time to the Minute
topics.short: Read and write times like 7:43 on a clock.
topics.trouble: When the minute hand is near 12, students read the hour hand as the next hour, saying 4:55 is 5:55.

topics.title: Elapsed Time
topics.short: Find how much time passes between two times.
topics.trouble: Students subtract times like ordinary numbers, so 10:10 minus 9:50 comes out as 60 minutes instead of 20.

topics.title: Mass and Liquid Volume
topics.short: Measure and solve problems in grams, kilograms and liters.
topics.trouble: Students mix up mass and size, thinking a big object must be heavier.

topics.title: Area with Unit Squares
topics.short: Area counts how many unit squares cover a shape.
topics.trouble: Students leave gaps or overlaps when tiling, or count units along the edge instead of squares inside.

topics.title: Area of a Rectangle by Multiplying
topics.short: Rows times squares in each row gives the area.

topics.title: Area and the Distributive Property
topics.short: Split a rectangle in two to find its area in parts.

topics.title: Area of L-Shaped Figures
topics.short: Break a shape into rectangles and add their areas.
topics.trouble: Students multiply the two longest sides of an L-shape as if it were a rectangle.

topics.title: Perimeter
topics.short: Add the side lengths to find the distance around.
topics.trouble: Students confuse area and perimeter, or count corner squares twice when finding the distance around.

topics.title: Finding a Missing Side
topics.short: Use the perimeter to find a side you don't know.

topics.title: Same Perimeter, Different Area
topics.short: Rectangles with the same perimeter can have different areas.
topics.trouble: Students assume two rectangles with the same perimeter must have the same area.

topics.title: Scaled Picture and Bar Graphs
topics.short: Read graphs where one symbol or one grid line stands for several.
topics.trouble: Students count each picture as 1 even when the key says each picture stands for 5.

topics.title: Measuring to the Nearest Half and Quarter Inch
topics.short: Read a ruler marked in halves and fourths.
topics.trouble: Students start measuring at the 1 mark, or read the tick count instead of the length.

topics.title: Line Plots with Halves and Fourths
topics.short: Show measurements as dots above a scale.

topics.title: Kinds of Quadrilaterals
topics.short: Rhombuses, rectangles and squares are all quadrilaterals.
topics.trouble: Students say a square is not a rectangle because it "looks different," instead of checking the attributes.

topics.title: Splitting Shapes into Equal Areas
topics.short: Each of 6 equal parts is 1/6 of the shape's area.
topics.trouble: Students think equal parts must have the same shape, not just the same area.
